name: Automated or absent post-application feedback
description: Absence of feedback, or delivery of generic automated feedback, after application submission or early assessment stages, without information that helps candidates understand the outcome or improve future applications.

name: Generic, contradictory, or seniority-misaligned job requirements
description: Job advertisements containing vague, contradictory, inflated, or seniority-incompatible requirements that prevent candidates from accurately understanding the role and calibrating their qualifications.

name: Unannounced changes to process format or schedule
description: Changes to interview format, process stages, schedule, or timeline introduced without prior communication or adequate explanation to candidates.

name: Negative reputation on review sites or social media
description: Negative information from review platforms, social media, or other external sources that undermines trust in the organization and influences candidates' willingness to proceed.

name: Late disclosure of contractual conditions
description: Late disclosure or omission of essential contractual information, such as salary, benefits, hiring model, work arrangement, or employer identity, until advanced stages of the recruitment process.

name: Use of corporate jargon and informal language in job postings
description: Use of corporate jargon, technical buzzwords, or informal expressions that obscure job expectations or make job postings difficult for candidates to understand.

name: Posting non-existent or ghost jobs
description: Publication or maintenance of vacancies that are inactive, already filled, or not intended for immediate hiring, creating false expectations among candidates.

name: Generic or unverifiable statements about organizational culture
description: Use of generic, superficial, or unverifiable statements about organizational culture and values that prevent candidates from understanding the actual work environment.

name: Standardized, template-based candidate communication
description: Use of impersonal, standardized, or template-based communications that discourage meaningful interaction and convey a lack of individual consideration toward candidates.

name: Delayed or omitted application status updates
description: Failure to provide timely, scheduled, or proactive updates about candidates' progression throughout the recruitment process.

name: Observed variation in process conditions across candidates
description: Differences in recruitment conditions, opportunities, or treatment observed across candidates, leading to perceptions of unequal procedural fairness.

name: Inquiries about personal characteristics unrelated to job qualifications
description: Questions, evaluation criteria, or decisions based on personal characteristics unrelated to job qualifications, such as gender, family status, appearance, geographic origin, or other non-job-related attributes.

name: Tests or practical activities disconnected from actual job responsibilities
description: Technical assessments whose content, format, or tasks do not reflect the actual responsibilities, tools, or competencies required for the target role.

name: Delayed or no feedback after interviews
description: Failure to provide timely feedback or any response after interviews, leaving candidates without closure regarding interview outcomes.

name: Omission of candidate-experience feedback mechanisms
description: Absence of mechanisms that allow candidates to provide feedback about their recruitment experience, preventing organizations from collecting information to improve their hiring practices.

name: Fully automated candidate interactions without human touchpoints
description: Recruitment processes in which candidate interactions rely almost exclusively on automated systems, without accessible human touchpoints for communication, clarification, or support.

name: Inconsistent assessment conditions across candidates
description: Application of inconsistent evaluation conditions, criteria, or assessment procedures across candidates, compromising perceptions of procedural fairness.

name: Misalignment between selection process stages and job competencies
description: Selection process stages or evaluation methods that fail to assess the competencies actually required for successful job performance.

name: Non-disclosure of evaluation criteria and rejection reasons
description: Failure to communicate the evaluation criteria, decision rationale, or rejection reasons used throughout the recruitment process.

name: Recruiter unfamiliarity with role-specific technical content
description: Recruiters demonstrating insufficient familiarity with the technical domain of the role, limiting their ability to explain requirements, conduct interviews, or evaluate candidates appropriately.

name: Unfulfilled promises
description: Failure to honor explicit commitments or expectations established during recruitment, including promises regarding compensation, career development, work conditions, or organizational culture.

name: Test complexity and deadlines disproportionate to the role's seniority level
description: Assignment of technical tests or take-home activities whose scope, complexity, or deadlines are disproportionate to the advertised seniority level or expected responsibilities of the position.

name: Formal degree or institution-prestige requirements unlinked to job tasks
description: Requirements for formal academic degrees or institutional prestige that are not necessary for performing the actual job responsibilities.

name: Job posting formats incompatible with assistive technologies
description: Job advertisements or recruitment materials presented in formats that are incompatible with assistive technologies or otherwise create unnecessary accessibility barriers for candidates with disabilities.

name: Technically inconsistent or impossible job requirements
description: Job advertisements containing technically inconsistent, contradictory, or impossible requirements that indicate poor alignment between recruitment practices and the realities of the technical role.
